newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares seen flat, incentives lacking.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares seen flat, incentives lacking.

text.p: Singapore shares were seen flat again on Wednesday with investors lacking the incentive to participate heavily in the market, dealers said.
"There's no real incentive to buy, but there's no real incentive to sell either," one dealer at a local firm said.
On Tuesday the key Straits Times Industrials Index ended almost unchanged at 2,061.22, up 0.32 point after spending much of the day in negative territory.
The influence of Wall Street was seen as one immediate short-term factor that could give Singapore stocks a boost, but dealers said they were also keeping a wary eye on it too.
"It's due for a correction, it's a matter of when," one dealer said.
